records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

fr.L: Et la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée, disant :
fr.B: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée :
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a donné ce message :

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 나에게 임하여 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 나에게 임했다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 이 말씀을 주셨다.

decisions.choice: the riddle of the two eagles and the vine, and its meaning
decisions.reason: The chapter has three parts: a riddle about two eagles, a cedar and a vine (verses 2-10); its meaning, King Zedekiah's broken oath to Babylon and his turn to Egypt (verses 11-21); and a promise that the LORD himself will plant a new cedar (verses 22-24).

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The formula follows the wording set in the Jeremiah table.

source.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם ח֥וּד חִידָ֖ה וּמְשֹׁ֣ל מָשָׁ֑ל אֶל־בֵּ֖ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Son of man, riddle a riddle and parable a parable to [the] house of Israel,

en.L: Son of man, propound a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel,
en.B: Son of man, pose a riddle and tell a parable to the house of Israel,
en.R: Son of man, tell the people of Israel a riddle, a story with a hidden meaning.

fr.L: Fils d’homme, propose une énigme et dis une parabole à la maison d’Israël,
fr.B: Fils d’homme, pose une énigme et raconte une parabole à la maison d’Israël,
fr.R: Fils d’homme, raconte au peuple d’Israël une énigme, une histoire au sens caché.

ko.L: 사람의 아들아, 이스라엘 집에 수수께끼를 내고 비유를 말하여라.
ko.B: 사람의 아들아, 이스라엘 집에 수수께끼를 내고 비유를 들려주어라.
ko.R: 사람의 아들아, 이스라엘 백성에게 수수께끼, 곧 숨은 뜻이 있는 이야기를 들려주어라.

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: a riddle and a parable: a story whose meaning must be worked out
decisions.reason: A riddle (*chidah*) hides its meaning (Judges 14:12-19), and a parable or saying (*mashal*) compares one thing with another. Here the two words describe one story, told in pictures, whose meaning is given in verses 11-21.

decisions.choice: a riddle, a story with a hidden meaning
decisions.reason: Readable gives one phrase for the two Hebrew words, since they name one story (m2), and "the people of Israel" for "the house of Israel".

decisions.choice: ’énigme’ and ’parabole’ (L, B); ’une énigme, une histoire au sens caché’ (R)
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew words are a pair (m2); ’parabole’ is the French word for mashal in the Gospels and keeps that link.

decisions.choice: "수수께끼" for chidah and "비유" for mashal
decisions.reason: Here mashal is a story with a hidden meaning, not a saying (as in 12:22 and 16:44, where it is 속담); R explains both words together, as the English R does.

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֞ כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הַנֶּ֤שֶׁר הַגָּדוֹל֙ גְּד֤וֹל הַכְּנָפַ֨יִם֙ אֶ֣רֶךְ הָאֵ֔בֶר מָלֵא֙ הַנּוֹצָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ל֖וֹ הָֽרִקְמָ֑ה בָּ֚א אֶל־הַלְּבָנ֔וֹן וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת־צַמֶּ֥רֶת הָאָֽרֶז׃

records.literal_gloss: and you will say, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: The great eagle, great of wings, long of pinion, full of plumage, which [had] many colors, came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar.

en.L: and say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: The great eagle, great of wings, long of pinions, full of plumage, which [had] many colors, came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar.
en.B: and say, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: A great eagle with great wings and long feathers, full of plumage of many colors, came to Lebanon and took hold of the top of the cedar.
en.R: Say to them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: A huge eagle came to Lebanon. It had great wings and long feathers of many colors. It took hold of the top of a cedar tree.

fr.L: et tu diras : Ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Le grand aigle, aux grandes ailes, aux longues pennes, plein de plumes, qui [avait] des couleurs variées, est venu au Liban et a pris la cime du cèdre.
fr.B: et dis : Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Un grand aigle aux grandes ailes et aux longues plumes, couvert d’un plumage de toutes les couleurs, est venu au Liban et a saisi la cime du cèdre.
fr.R: Dis-leur : Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Un immense aigle est venu au Liban. Il avait de grandes ailes et de longues plumes de toutes les couleurs. Il a saisi la cime d’un cèdre.

ko.L: 말하여라. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 날개가 크고 깃이 길며, 여러 빛깔의 깃털이 가득한 큰 독수리가 레바논에 와서 백향목 꼭대기를 잡았다.
ko.B: 이렇게 말하여라. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 날개가 크고 깃이 길며, 알록달록한 깃털로 뒤덮인 큰 독수리 한 마리가 레바논으로 날아와 백향목 꼭대기를 움켜잡았다.
ko.R: 그들에게 이렇게 말하여라. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 아주 큰 독수리 한 마리가 레바논으로 날아왔다. 그 독수리는 날개가 크고, 여러 빛깔의 긴 깃털이 있었다. 그 독수리가 백향목 꼭대기를 움켜잡았다.

decisions.choice: the great eagle: the king of Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: Verse 12 explains the picture: the eagle is the king of Babylon. The eagle, with its huge wings and splendid feathers, pictures his power and the reach of his empire (compare Jeremiah 48:40; 49:22). The bird may be an eagle or a large vulture; the same word is used for both.

decisions.choice: Lebanon ... the top of the cedar: the royal house in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The cedars of Lebanon were the finest trees of the region, and Solomon's palace was called "the House of the Forest of Lebanon" for its cedar pillars (1 Kings 7:2). Jeremiah speaks to the royal house in Jerusalem as "you who live in Lebanon, nested in the cedars" (Jeremiah 22:23). The top of the cedar is the king, as verse 12 says.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. Under the quotation rule for Ezekiel, the LORD's words and the message Ezekiel is told to give take no quotation marks; only human speech quoted inside them takes double quotes.

decisions.choice: "독수리" for the eagle (nesher) and "백향목" for the cedar
decisions.reason: The established Korean words, as in Exodus 19:4 and 1 Kings 5; the riddle keeps its images at every level, and the meaning is given in 17:12-21.

source.text: אֵ֛ת רֹ֥אשׁ יְנִֽיקוֹתָ֖יו קָטָ֑ף וַיְבִיאֵ֨הוּ֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן בְּעִ֥יר רֹכְלִ֖ים שָׂמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: The top of its young twigs it plucked off, and it brought it to a land of merchants; in a city of traders it set it.

en.L: The topmost of its young twigs it plucked off and brought it to a land of merchants; it set it in a city of traders.
en.B: It plucked off the topmost of its young shoots and carried it to a land of merchants, and it set it down in a city of traders.
en.R: It broke off the highest young branch and carried it away to a land of traders. It put it down in a city of merchants.

fr.L: Le plus haut de ses jeunes rameaux, il l’a arraché et l’a emporté dans un pays de marchands ; il l’a placé dans une ville de commerçants.
fr.B: Il a arraché le plus haut de ses jeunes rameaux et l’a emporté dans un pays de marchands, et il l’a déposé dans une ville de commerçants.
fr.R: Il a cassé la plus haute de ses jeunes branches et l’a emportée dans un pays de commerçants. Il l’a déposée dans une ville de marchands.

ko.L: 그것이 그 어린 가지들의 맨 꼭대기를 꺾어 상인들의 땅으로 가져가서, 장사꾼들의 성읍에 두었다.
ko.B: 그 독수리는 맨 꼭대기의 어린 가지를 꺾어 상인들의 땅으로 가져가서 장사꾼들의 성읍에 두었다.
ko.R: 그 독수리는 가장 높은 곳에 있는 어린 가지를 꺾어서 장사하는 사람들의 땅으로 가져갔다. 그리고 그것을 상인들의 성읍에 두었다.

decisions.choice: the topmost shoot carried off: King Jehoiachin taken to Babylon in 597 BC
decisions.reason: Verse 12 says that the king of Babylon took Jerusalem's king and officials to Babylon. This is Jehoiachin, who was taken there with the leading people of Jerusalem after a reign of three months (2 Kings 24:8-16). Ezekiel himself was taken into exile at the same time (1:2).

decisions.choice: a land of merchants: the word Canaan, used for "traders", here Babylonia
decisions.reason: As in 16:29, the word *kena'an* means traders. Babylon was a city of great trade.

source.text: וַיִּקַּח֙ מִזֶּ֣רַע הָאָ֔רֶץ וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖הוּ בִּשְׂדֵה־זָ֑רַע קָ֚ח עַל־מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים צַפְצָפָ֖ה שָׂמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it took from the seed of the land and put it in a field of seed; [as] a shoot by many waters, [as] a willow it set it.

en.L: Then it took some of the seed of the land and put it in a field for sowing; [as] a shoot beside abundant waters, [like] a willow it set it.
en.B: Then it took a seed from the land and planted it in a fertile field. It set it like a willow shoot beside abundant water.
en.R: Then it took a seed from the land itself and planted it in a good field. It planted it beside plenty of water, the way a willow is planted.

fr.L: Puis il a pris de la semence du pays et l’a mise dans un champ à semer ; [comme] une pousse près des eaux abondantes, [comme] un saule il l’a placée.
fr.B: Puis il a pris une semence du pays et l’a plantée dans un champ fertile. Il l’a placée comme une bouture de saule au bord d’eaux abondantes.
fr.R: Puis il a pris une graine du pays lui-même et l’a plantée dans un bon champ. Il l’a plantée au bord de beaucoup d’eau, comme on plante un saule.

ko.L: 그리고 그것이 그 땅의 씨 가운데서 얼마를 가져다가 씨 뿌릴 밭에 두었다. 물이 많은 곳 곁에 [둔] 싹처럼, 버드나무처럼 그것을 심었다.
ko.B: 그러고는 그 땅의 씨 하나를 가져다가 기름진 밭에 심었다. 물이 많은 곳 곁에 버드나무 가지를 심듯이 그것을 심었다.
ko.R: 그다음에 그 독수리는 그 땅에서 씨 하나를 가져다가 좋은 밭에 심었다. 버드나무를 심듯이 물이 넉넉한 곳 곁에 그것을 심었다.

decisions.choice: the seed of the land: a member of Judah's royal family, Zedekiah
decisions.reason: Verse 13 explains that the king of Babylon took "one of the royal offspring" and made a covenant with him. This is Zedekiah, Jehoiachin's uncle, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king in 597 BC (2 Kings 24:17). Unlike the cedar's top, he was left in his own land.

decisions.choice: a shoot ... a willow: words of uncertain meaning
alternatives: he took it beside many waters
decisions.reason: The word taken as "shoot" may also be read as a verb, "he took", and the word taken as "willow" is found only here. Either way, the seedling is planted where it can grow well.

decisions.choice: a seed from the land itself
alternatives: a seed of the land of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the contrast with the cedar top, which was carried away: this seed came from the land and was planted there.

source.text: וַיִּצְמַ֡ח וַיְהִי֩ לְגֶ֨פֶן סֹרַ֜חַת שִׁפְלַ֣ת קוֹמָ֗ה לִפְנ֤וֹת דָּלִיּוֹתָיו֙ אֵלָ֔יו וְשָׁרָשָׁ֖יו תַּחְתָּ֣יו יִֽהְי֑וּ וַתְּהִ֣י לְגֶ֔פֶן וַתַּ֣עַשׂ בַּדִּ֔ים וַתְּשַׁלַּ֖ח פֹּארֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it sprouted and became a spreading vine, low of stature, its branches turning toward it and its roots under it were; and it became a vine and produced shoots and sent out boughs.

en.L: And it sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height, its branches turning toward it, and its roots were under it; so it became a vine and produced shoots and sent out boughs.
en.B: It sprouted and became a low, spreading vine. Its branches turned toward the eagle, and its roots stayed under it. So it became a vine, producing shoots and sending out branches.
en.R: The seed sprouted and grew into a vine. It spread out low on the ground. Its branches turned toward the eagle, and its roots stayed under the eagle. So it became a vine with many shoots and branches.

fr.L: Et elle a germé et est devenue une vigne qui s’étale, basse de taille, ses branches tournées vers lui, et ses racines étaient sous lui ; elle est devenue une vigne, elle a produit des pousses et étendu des rameaux.
fr.B: Elle a germé et est devenue une vigne basse qui s’étalait. Ses branches se tournaient vers l’aigle, et ses racines restaient sous lui. Elle est donc devenue une vigne, produisant des pousses et étendant ses rameaux.
fr.R: La graine a germé et elle est devenue une vigne. Elle s’étalait au ras du sol. Ses branches se tournaient vers l’aigle, et ses racines restaient sous l’aigle. Elle est devenue une vigne avec beaucoup de pousses et de branches.

ko.L: 그리고 그것이 싹이 나서 키가 낮고 넓게 퍼지는 포도나무가 되었다. 그 가지들은 그것을 향하고, 그 뿌리들은 그 아래에 있었다. 그리하여 그것이 포도나무가 되어 가지를 내고 잎을 피웠다.
ko.B: 그 씨가 싹이 나서 낮게 퍼지는 포도나무가 되었다. 그 가지들은 독수리를 향하고, 뿌리들은 독수리 아래에 머물러 있었다. 이렇게 그것은 포도나무가 되어 가지를 내고 덩굴을 뻗었다.
ko.R: 그 씨가 싹이 나서 포도나무로 자랐다. 그 나무는 땅에 낮게 퍼졌다. 그 가지들은 독수리 쪽으로 뻗었고, 뿌리들은 독수리 아래에 머물러 있었다. 그렇게 그것은 가지와 덩굴이 많은 포도나무가 되었다.

decisions.choice: its branches turning toward it, its roots under it: the vine turns to the eagle and stays under its power
decisions.reason: "Toward it" refers to the eagle. "Under it" probably does too: the vine's roots are under the eagle's control. Some read it as the vine's own roots. The picture is of a small kingdom that flourishes because it stays loyal to Babylon (verse 14).

decisions.choice: toward the eagle (B, R); under the eagle (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the eagle so that the reader does not take "it" to be the vine (m1). Balanced leaves "under it" as the Hebrew has it.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י נֶֽשֶׁר־אֶחָד֙ גָּד֔וֹל גְּד֥וֹל כְּנָפַ֖יִם וְרַב־נוֹצָ֑ה וְהִנֵּה֩ הַגֶּ֨פֶן הַזֹּ֜את כָּֽפְנָ֧ה שָׁרֳשֶׁ֣יהָ עָלָ֗יו וְדָֽלִיּוֹתָיו֙ שִׁלְחָה־לּ֔וֹ לְהַשְׁק֣וֹת אוֹתָ֔הּ מֵעֲרֻג֖וֹת מַטָּעָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And there was one great eagle, great of wings and great of plumage; and look, this vine bent its roots toward it, and its branches it sent out toward it, to water it, from the beds of its planting.

en.L: And there was another great eagle, great of wings and great of plumage; and look, this vine bent its roots toward it and sent out its branches toward it, that it might water it, from the beds where it was planted.
en.B: But there was another great eagle with great wings and thick plumage. And look, this vine bent its roots toward it and stretched out its branches to it from the beds where it was planted, so that it might water it.
en.R: But there was another huge eagle with great wings and thick feathers. And the vine turned its roots toward this eagle. It reached out its branches to it, away from the garden bed where it was planted, hoping the eagle would give it more water.

fr.L: Et il y avait un autre grand aigle, aux grandes ailes et au plumage abondant ; et voici, cette vigne a tourné ses racines vers lui et a étendu ses rameaux vers lui, pour qu’il l’arrose, loin des plates-bandes où elle était plantée.
fr.B: Mais il y avait un autre grand aigle aux grandes ailes et au plumage épais. Et voici que cette vigne a tourné ses racines vers lui et a tendu ses rameaux vers lui, loin des plates-bandes où elle était plantée, pour qu’il l’arrose.
fr.R: Mais il y avait un autre aigle immense, avec de grandes ailes et des plumes épaisses. Et la vigne a tourné ses racines vers cet aigle. Elle a tendu ses branches vers lui, loin du jardin où elle était plantée, en espérant qu’il lui donnerait plus d’eau.

ko.L: 그리고 날개가 크고 깃털이 많은 또 다른 큰 독수리가 있었다. 그런데 보아라, 이 포도나무가 그 독수리가 자기에게 물을 대어 주기를 바라고, 자기가 심긴 두둑에서 그것을 향하여 뿌리를 구부리고 가지를 뻗었다.
ko.B: 그런데 날개가 크고 깃털이 무성한 또 다른 큰 독수리 한 마리가 있었다. 그러자 이 포도나무가 자기가 심긴 두둑에서 그 독수리를 향하여 뿌리를 뻗고 가지를 내밀었다. 그 독수리가 물을 대어 주기를 바란 것이다.
ko.R: 그런데 날개가 크고 깃털이 무성한 또 다른 큰 독수리가 있었다. 그러자 그 포도나무는 이 독수리 쪽으로 뿌리를 돌렸다. 자기가 심긴 밭에서 이 독수리 쪽으로 가지를 뻗었다. 이 독수리가 물을 더 많이 대어 주기를 바란 것이다.

decisions.choice: another great eagle: the king of Egypt
decisions.reason: Verse 15 explains that Zedekiah sent to Egypt for horses and troops. The second eagle is Pharaoh, probably Hophra (Apries), who sent an army that briefly lifted the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem (Jeremiah 37:5-11; 44:30).

decisions.choice: one great eagle: another eagle
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "one great eagle", meaning "another", as the Hebrew word for "one" can (compare 10:9).

decisions.choice: hoping the eagle would give it more water
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the vine already had water where it was planted (verse 8), so it was looking for more.

source.text: אֶל־שָׂ֥דֶה טּ֛וֹב אֶל־מַ֥יִם רַבִּ֖ים הִ֣יא שְׁתוּלָ֑ה לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת עָנָף֙ וְלָשֵׂ֣את פֶּ֔רִי לִהְי֖וֹת לְגֶ֥פֶן אַדָּֽרֶת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: In a good field by many waters it [was] planted, to produce branches and to bear fruit, to become a splendid vine.

en.L: In a good field beside abundant waters it had been planted, to produce branches and to bear fruit, to become a splendid vine.
en.B: Yet it had been planted in good soil beside abundant water, where it could produce branches, bear fruit and become a splendid vine.
en.R: But it had already been planted in a good field with plenty of water. There it could have grown branches and fruit and become a beautiful vine.

fr.L: Dans un bon champ, près des eaux abondantes, elle avait été plantée, pour produire des rameaux et porter du fruit, pour devenir une vigne magnifique.
fr.B: Pourtant, elle avait été plantée dans une bonne terre, au bord d’eaux abondantes, où elle pouvait produire des rameaux, porter du fruit et devenir une vigne magnifique.
fr.R: Pourtant, elle avait déjà été plantée dans un bon champ avec beaucoup d’eau. Là, elle aurait pu faire des branches et des fruits et devenir une belle vigne.

ko.L: 그것은 가지를 내고 열매를 맺어 훌륭한 포도나무가 되도록, 물이 많은 곳 곁의 좋은 밭에 심겨 있었다.
ko.B: 그 포도나무는 이미 물이 넉넉한 좋은 땅에 심겨 있어서, 가지를 내고 열매를 맺어 훌륭한 포도나무가 될 수 있었다.
ko.R: 그러나 그 포도나무는 이미 물이 넉넉한 좋은 밭에 심겨 있었다. 거기서 가지를 내고 열매를 맺어 아름다운 포도나무가 될 수 있었다.

decisions.choice: it had been planted in a good field: it had no need to turn to the second eagle
decisions.reason: The point of the riddle is here: the vine was already well placed. Under Babylon, Zedekiah's small kingdom could have lasted (verse 14). Its turn to Egypt was not need but disloyalty.

source.text: אֱמֹ֗ר כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִ֖ה תִּצְלָ֑ח הֲלוֹא֩ אֶת־שָׁרָשֶׁ֨יהָ יְנַתֵּ֜ק וְאֶת־פִּרְיָ֣הּ׀יְקוֹסֵ֣ס וְיָבֵ֗שׁ כָּל־טַרְפֵּ֤י צִמְחָהּ֙ תִּיבָ֔שׁ וְלֹֽא־בִזְרֹ֤עַ גְּדוֹלָה֙ וּבְעַם־רָ֔ב לְמַשְׂא֥וֹת אוֹתָ֖הּ מִשָּׁרָשֶֽׁיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Say, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Will it prosper? Its roots will he not tear up, and its fruit strip off, so that it withers, all the fresh leaves of its sprouting wither? And not with a great arm and with many people [will he need] to lift it from its roots.

en.L: Say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Will it prosper? Will he not tear up its roots and strip off its fruit, so that it withers, all its fresh sprouting leaves wither? And not with a great arm or with many people [will he need] to lift it up by its roots.
en.B: Say, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Will it thrive? Will the first eagle not tear up its roots and strip off its fruit, so that it withers? All its fresh new leaves will wither. He will need no strong arm or great army to pull it up by its roots.
en.R: Then say to them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Will that vine grow well? No! The first eagle will pull it up by the roots and strip off its fruit, and it will dry up. All its new leaves will dry up. He will not need a strong army or many people to pull it up by its roots.

fr.L: Dis : Ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Prospérera-t-elle ? Ne va-t-il pas arracher ses racines et dépouiller son fruit, pour qu’elle sèche, que sèchent toutes les feuilles fraîches de ses pousses ? Et il ne [faudra] pas un grand bras ni un peuple nombreux pour la soulever de ses racines.
fr.B: Dis : Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Va-t-elle prospérer ? Le premier aigle ne va-t-il pas arracher ses racines et dépouiller ses fruits, pour qu’elle se dessèche ? Toutes ses jeunes feuilles se dessécheront. Il ne lui faudra ni bras puissant ni grande armée pour l’arracher avec ses racines.
fr.R: Puis dis-leur : Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Cette vigne va-t-elle bien pousser ? Non ! Le premier aigle va l’arracher avec ses racines et enlever ses fruits, et elle va se dessécher. Toutes ses nouvelles feuilles vont sécher. Il n’aura pas besoin d’une armée puissante ni de beaucoup de gens pour l’arracher avec ses racines.

ko.L: 말하여라. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 그것이 잘되겠느냐? 그가 그 뿌리를 뽑고 그 열매를 따 버려서, 그것이 시들지 않겠느냐? 새로 돋은 그 싱싱한 잎이 다 시들지 않겠느냐? 그것을 뿌리째 뽑아 올리는 데 큰 팔이나 많은 백성이 [필요하지] 않을 것이다.
ko.B: 말하여라. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 그 포도나무가 잘 자라겠느냐? 첫째 독수리가 그 뿌리를 뽑고 열매를 따 버려서 그것을 말라 죽게 하지 않겠느냐? 새로 돋은 싱싱한 잎이 모두 시들 것이다. 그것을 뿌리째 뽑는 데에는 강한 팔도 많은 군대도 필요 없을 것이다.
ko.R: 그다음에 그들에게 말하여라. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 그 포도나무가 잘 자라겠느냐? 아니다! 첫째 독수리가 그것을 뿌리째 뽑고 열매를 따 버릴 것이다. 그러면 그 나무는 말라 버릴 것이다. 새로 난 잎도 모두 말라 버릴 것이다. 그것을 뿌리째 뽑는 데에는 강한 군대도 많은 사람도 필요 없을 것이다.

decisions.choice: will he not tear up: the first eagle, the king of Babylon, will destroy the vine
alternatives: will one not tear it up
will it not be torn up
decisions.reason: The subject of "tear up" is not named. It is probably the first eagle, who planted the vine and will punish its disloyalty, as verses 16-20 explain. The verb can also be read without a subject, "will it not be torn up".

decisions.choice: not with a great arm or many people: it will take no great effort
decisions.reason: "Arm" stands for strength. The vine is so weak that it will be pulled up easily.

decisions.choice: the first eagle (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who "he" is (m1).

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֥ה שְׁתוּלָ֖ה הֲתִצְלָ֑ח הֲלוֹא֩ כְגַ֨עַת בָּ֜הּ ר֤וּחַ הַקָּדִים֙ תִּיבַ֣שׁ יָבֹ֔שׁ עַל־עֲרֻגֹ֥ת צִמְחָ֖הּ תִּיבָֽשׁ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And look, [it is] planted; will it prosper? Will it not, when the east wind touches it, wither completely? On the beds of its sprouting it will wither.

en.L: And look, [though] planted, will it prosper? When the east wind touches it, will it not utterly wither? On the beds where it sprouted it will wither.
en.B: Look, it is planted, but will it thrive? Will it not wither completely when the east wind strikes it? It will wither in the beds where it sprouted.
en.R: It is planted, but will it grow well? No! When the hot east wind blows on it, it will dry up completely. It will dry up right there in the garden bed where it grew.

fr.L: Et voici, [bien que] plantée, prospérera-t-elle ? Quand le vent d’est la touchera, ne séchera-t-elle pas complètement ? Sur les plates-bandes où elle a germé, elle séchera.
fr.B: La voici plantée, mais va-t-elle prospérer ? Ne se desséchera-t-elle pas complètement quand le vent d’est la frappera ? Elle se desséchera dans les plates-bandes où elle a poussé.
fr.R: Elle est plantée, mais va-t-elle bien pousser ? Non ! Quand le vent brûlant de l’est soufflera sur elle, elle séchera complètement. Elle séchera là même, dans le jardin où elle a poussé.

ko.L: 보아라, [그것이] 심겼으나 잘되겠느냐? 동풍이 그것에 닿으면 아주 시들지 않겠느냐? 그것이 싹 튼 두둑에서 시들 것이다.
ko.B: 그것이 심기기는 했으나 잘 자라겠느냐? 동풍이 불어닥치면 아주 시들어 버리지 않겠느냐? 그것은 싹이 튼 바로 그 두둑에서 시들어 버릴 것이다.
ko.R: 그 나무는 심기기는 했지만 잘 자라겠느냐? 아니다! 뜨거운 동풍이 불면 그 나무는 완전히 말라 버릴 것이다. 자라던 그 밭에서 그대로 말라 버릴 것이다.

decisions.choice: the east wind: the hot, dry wind from the desert, a picture of Babylon's attack
decisions.reason: The east wind blows from the desert and withers plants in a day (Genesis 41:6; Hosea 13:15). Here it pictures the army of Babylon, which lay to the east.

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

fr.L: Et la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée, disant :
fr.B: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée :
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a donné ce message :

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 나에게 임하여 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 나에게 임했다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 이 말씀을 주셨다.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me (all levels, as verse 1)
decisions.reason: The settled formula, worded exactly as in verse 1 and in 1-7.

source.text: אֱמָר־נָא֙ לְבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔רִי הֲלֹ֥א יְדַעְתֶּ֖ם מָה־אֵ֑לֶּה אֱמֹ֗ר הִנֵּה־בָ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֤ל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־מַלְכָּהּ֙ וְאֶת־שָׂרֶ֔יהָ וַיָּבֵ֥א אוֹתָ֛ם אֵלָ֖יו בָּבֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Say now to the house of rebellion: Do you not know what these [are]? Say: Look, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and took its king and its officials and brought them to himself to Babylon.

en.L: Say now to the house of rebellion, "Do you not know what these [mean]?" Say, Look, the king of Babylon has come to Jerusalem and has taken its king and its officials and brought them to himself to Babylon.
en.B: Ask the rebellious house, "Do you not know what these things mean?" Then tell them, The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took its king and its officials, and brought them back with him to Babylon.
en.R: Say to these people who refuse to obey, "Do you not understand what this story means?" Then tell them, The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem. He took its king and its leaders and brought them with him to Babylon.

fr.L: Dis donc à la maison de rébellion : « Ne savez-vous pas ce que [signifient] ces [choses] ? » Dis : Voici, le roi de Babylone est venu à Jérusalem, il a pris son roi et ses chefs et les a emmenés auprès de lui à Babylone.
fr.B: Demande à la maison rebelle : « Ne savez-vous pas ce que cela signifie ? » Puis dis-leur : Le roi de Babylone est venu à Jérusalem, il a pris son roi et ses chefs et les a emmenés avec lui à Babylone.
fr.R: Dis à ce peuple qui refuse d’obéir : « Ne comprenez-vous pas ce que veut dire cette histoire ? » Puis dis-leur : Le roi de Babylone est venu à Jérusalem. Il a pris son roi et ses dirigeants et les a emmenés avec lui à Babylone.

ko.L: 이제 반역의 집에게 "너희는 이것들이 무엇인지 알지 못하느냐?" 하고 말하여라. 말하여라. 보아라, 바빌론 왕이 예루살렘에 와서 그 왕과 고관들을 잡아 바빌론으로 자기에게 데려갔다.
ko.B: 반역하는 족속에게 "너희는 이것들이 무슨 뜻인지 모르느냐?" 하고 물어라. 그리고 말하여라. 바빌론 왕이 예루살렘에 와서 그 왕과 관리들을 사로잡아 바빌론으로 끌고 갔다.
ko.R: 말을 듣지 않는 이 백성에게 "너희는 이 이야기가 무슨 뜻인지 모르느냐?" 하고 물어라. 그리고 말하여라. 바빌론 왕이 예루살렘에 왔다. 그는 그 나라의 왕과 지도자들을 사로잡아 바빌론으로 끌고 갔다.

decisions.choice: the house of rebellion: Israel, a people who refuse to obey
decisions.reason: This is Ezekiel's name for his people (see the main note at 2:5).

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem: the surrender of 597 BC
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem in 597 BC. King Jehoiachin surrendered and was taken to Babylon with his mother, his officials and many leading people (2 Kings 24:10-16). This explains the cedar top of verses 3-4.

decisions.choice: the house of rebellion (L); the rebellious house (B); people who refuse to obey (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *bet meri* in Ezekiel.

decisions.choice: officials (L, B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *sar*.

decisions.choice: ’chefs’ (L, B); ’dirigeants’ (R) for sarim, for the whole book
decisions.reason: The prophets’ term list; ’prince’ stays for nasi.

decisions.choice: "고관" (L), "관리" (B), "지도자" (R) for sarim
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording, as Jeremiah 38:4.

source.text: וַיִּקַּח֙ מִזֶּ֣רַע הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה וַיִּכְרֹ֥ת אִתּ֖וֹ בְּרִ֑ית וַיָּבֵ֤א אֹתוֹ֙ בְּאָלָ֔ה וְאֶת־אֵילֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ לָקָֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: And he took one of the seed of the kingdom and made with him a covenant and brought him into an oath; and the mighty of the land he took,

en.L: And he took one of the royal offspring and made a covenant with him and put him under an oath; and the mighty of the land he took away,
en.B: He took a member of the royal family, made a covenant with him and put him under oath. He also took away the leading men of the land,
en.R: He took a man from the royal family and made an agreement with him. He made him swear to be loyal. He also took away the most powerful men of the land.

fr.L: Et il a pris quelqu’un de la descendance royale, il a conclu une alliance avec lui et l’a fait entrer sous serment ; et les puissants du pays, il les a emmenés,
fr.B: Il a pris un membre de la famille royale, il a conclu une alliance avec lui et l’a lié par un serment. Il a aussi emmené les hommes influents du pays,
fr.R: Il a pris un homme de la famille royale et il a conclu un accord avec lui. Il lui a fait jurer d’être loyal. Il a aussi emmené les hommes les plus puissants du pays.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 왕의 혈통 가운데서 한 사람을 데려다가 그와 언약을 맺고 그에게 맹세를 시켰다. 그리고 그 땅의 권세 있는 자들을 데려갔으니,
ko.B: 그리고 왕족 가운데 한 사람을 데려다가 그와 언약을 맺고 그에게 맹세를 시켰다. 또 그 땅의 지도층 사람들도 끌고 갔다.
ko.R: 그리고 그는 왕족 가운데 한 사람을 골라 그와 조약을 맺었다. 그에게 충성하겠다고 맹세하게 했다. 또 그 땅에서 힘 있는 사람들을 끌고 갔다.

decisions.choice: one of the royal offspring: Zedekiah, made king under oath to Babylon
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place and renamed him Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:17). Zedekiah swore loyalty to Nebuchadnezzar in the name of God (2 Chronicles 36:13). This explains the seed planted in verse 5.

decisions.choice: a covenant: a treaty between a great king and a subject king
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the covenant between the LORD and Israel and for treaties between kings. Here it is a treaty in which Zedekiah promised to serve Babylon. Verse 19 calls it the LORD's covenant, because it was sworn in his name.

decisions.choice: an agreement
decisions.reason: Readable uses "agreement" for this treaty between kings, so that it is not confused with the LORD's covenant with Israel, and "swear to be loyal" for the oath.

decisions.choice: ’un accord’ (R), ’une alliance’ (L, B) for this treaty
decisions.reason: As the English Readable ’agreement’: the word is the same as God’s covenant, but here it names a treaty between kings.

decisions.choice: "조약" (R) for berit as a treaty between kings, where L and B keep "언약"
decisions.reason: The English R says "agreement"; 조약 is the plain Korean for a treaty, and L and B keep 언약 so that "my covenant" in 17:19 stays linked.

source.text: לִֽהְיוֹת֙ מַמְלָכָ֣ה שְׁפָלָ֔ה לְבִלְתִּ֖י הִתְנַשֵּׂ֑א לִשְׁמֹ֥ר אֶת־בְּרִית֖וֹ לְעָמְדָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: to be a lowly kingdom, not to lift itself up, to keep his covenant, so that it might stand.

en.L: that the kingdom might be lowly, not lifting itself up, keeping his covenant so that it might stand.
en.B: so that the kingdom would stay lowly and not rise up again, but would keep his covenant and so survive.
en.R: He did this so that the kingdom would stay weak and not rebel. If it kept the agreement, it would survive.

fr.L: pour que le royaume soit humble, sans s’élever, gardant son alliance pour subsister.
fr.B: pour que le royaume reste humble et ne se relève pas, mais qu’il garde son alliance et survive ainsi.
fr.R: Il a fait cela pour que le royaume reste faible et ne se révolte pas. S’il respectait l’accord, il survivrait.

ko.L: 그 나라를 낮추어 스스로 일어서지 못하게 하고, 그의 언약을 지켜야 [그 나라가] 서 있게 하려는 것이었다.
ko.B: 그 나라를 약하게 하여 다시 일어서지 못하게 하고, 그와 맺은 언약을 지켜야만 살아남을 수 있게 하려는 것이었다.
ko.R: 그가 이렇게 한 것은 그 나라를 약하게 하여 반역하지 못하게 하려는 것이었다. 그 나라는 조약을 지켜야만 살아남을 수 있었다.

decisions.choice: to keep his covenant so that it might stand: the kingdom could survive by keeping the treaty
decisions.reason: "His covenant" is the covenant the king of Babylon made (verse 13). As long as Judah kept it, the kingdom would go on, as the riddle's well-planted vine shows (verse 8). Jeremiah gave the same advice (Jeremiah 27:12-17).

source.text: וַיִּמְרָד־בּ֗וֹ לִשְׁלֹ֤חַ מַלְאָכָיו֙ מִצְרַ֔יִם לָֽתֶת־ל֥וֹ סוּסִ֖ים וְעַם־רָ֑ב הֲיִצְלָ֤ח הֲיִמָּלֵט֙ הָעֹשֵׂ֣ה אֵ֔לֶּה וְהֵפֵ֥ר בְּרִ֖ית וְנִמְלָֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: But he rebelled against him by sending his messengers [to] Egypt, to give him horses and many people. Will he prosper? Will he escape, the one doing these [things]? And will he break a covenant and escape?

en.L: But he rebelled against him by sending his messengers [to] Egypt, so that it would give him horses and a numerous people. Will he prosper? Will he escape, the one who does these [things]? Can he break a covenant and escape?
en.B: But he rebelled against him by sending envoys to Egypt to get horses and a large army. Will he succeed? Will a man who does such things escape? Can he break a covenant and still escape?
en.R: But the new king rebelled against the king of Babylon. He sent messengers to Egypt, asking for horses and a large army. Will he succeed? Will a man who does this get away with it? Can he break an agreement and still escape?

fr.L: Mais il s’est révolté contre lui en envoyant ses messagers [en] Égypte, pour qu’elle lui donne des chevaux et un peuple nombreux. Prospérera-t-il ? Échappera-t-il, celui qui fait ces [choses] ? Rompra-t-il l’alliance et échappera-t-il ?
fr.B: Mais il s’est révolté contre lui en envoyant des messagers en Égypte pour obtenir des chevaux et une grande armée. Réussira-t-il ? Celui qui agit ainsi échappera-t-il ? Peut-il rompre une alliance et s’en tirer ?
fr.R: Mais le nouveau roi s’est révolté contre le roi de Babylone. Il a envoyé des messagers en Égypte pour demander des chevaux et une grande armée. Va-t-il réussir ? Un homme qui fait cela va-t-il s’en tirer ? Peut-il rompre un accord et s’échapper quand même ?

ko.L: 그러나 그는 이집트에 자기 사신들을 보내어 말들과 많은 군대를 달라고 하여 그를 배반했다. 그가 잘되겠느냐? 이런 일을 하는 자가 피할 수 있겠느냐? 언약을 깨고도 피할 수 있겠느냐?
ko.B: 그러나 그는 이집트에 사신들을 보내어 말들과 많은 군대를 얻으려고 하여 바빌론 왕을 배반했다. 그가 성공하겠느냐? 이런 짓을 하는 자가 무사하겠느냐? 언약을 깨뜨리고도 벌을 피할 수 있겠느냐?
ko.R: 그러나 새 왕은 바빌론 왕을 배반했다. 그는 이집트에 사신들을 보내어 말들과 많은 군대를 보내 달라고 했다. 그가 성공하겠느냐? 이런 짓을 한 사람이 무사하겠느냐? 조약을 깨뜨리고도 벌을 피할 수 있겠느냐?

decisions.choice: he rebelled against him by sending to Egypt: Zedekiah's revolt against Babylon
decisions.reason: Zedekiah rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar (2 Kings 24:20), relying on help from Egypt. The Babylonians besieged Jerusalem from 588 BC, and the city fell in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:1-4).

decisions.choice: horses: the Law warned the king not to go back to Egypt for horses
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 17:16 forbids the king to send people to Egypt to get horses, and Isaiah 31:1 condemns those who go down to Egypt for help and rely on horses.

decisions.choice: the new king ... the king of Babylon
decisions.reason: Readable names the two kings, since the Hebrew pronouns could confuse.

source.text: חַי־אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ אִם־לֹ֗א בִּמְקוֹם֙ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַמַּמְלִ֣יךְ אֹת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּזָה֙ אֶת־אָ֣לָת֔וֹ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵפֵ֖ר אֶת־בְּרִית֑וֹ אִתּ֥וֹ בְתוֹךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל יָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: [As] I live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, surely in the place of the king who made him king, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, with him in the midst of Babylon he will die.

en.L: [As] I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, surely in the place of the king who caused him to reign, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, with him in the midst of Babylon he will die.
en.B: As surely as I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, it is in Babylon that he will die, in the land of the king who put him on the throne, the king whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke.
en.R: As surely as I live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, he will die in Babylon. He will die in the land of the king who made him king. He despised the promise he made to that king and broke their agreement.

fr.L: [Aussi vrai que] je suis vivant, déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, c’est dans le lieu du roi qui l’a fait régner, dont il a méprisé le serment et dont il a rompu l’alliance, auprès de lui, au milieu de Babylone, qu’il mourra.
fr.B: Aussi vrai que je suis vivant, déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, c’est à Babylone qu’il mourra, dans le pays du roi qui l’a mis sur le trône, le roi dont il a méprisé le serment et rompu l’alliance.
fr.R: Aussi vrai que je suis vivant, dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, il mourra à Babylone. Il mourra dans le pays du roi qui l’a fait roi. Il a méprisé la promesse qu’il avait faite à ce roi et il a rompu leur accord.

ko.L: 내가 살아 있음을 [두고 맹세한다]. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}의 선언이다. 그를 왕으로 세운 그 왕, 곧 그가 맹세를 업신여기고 언약을 깨뜨린 그 왕이 있는 곳, 바빌론 한가운데서 그가 그 왕과 함께 죽을 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 살아 있음을 두고 맹세한다. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}의 말이다. 그는 바빌론에서 죽을 것이다. 그를 왕으로 세운 그 왕의 땅, 그가 맹세를 업신여기고 언약을 깨뜨린 그 왕의 땅에서 죽을 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 살아 있음을 두고 맹세한다. 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}의 말이다. 그는 바빌론에서 죽을 것이다. 자기를 왕으로 세운 왕의 땅에서 죽을 것이다. 그는 그 왕에게 한 맹세를 하찮게 여기고 그 왕과 맺은 조약을 깨뜨렸다.

decisions.choice: in Babylon he will die: Zedekiah's end
decisions.reason: When Jerusalem fell, Zedekiah fled and was captured. His sons were killed before his eyes, he was blinded and taken to Babylon, and he died there (2 Kings 25:4-7; Jeremiah 52:11).

decisions.choice: As I live, declares the Lord GOD (L); As surely as I live (B, R)
decisions.reason: The oath follows the wording set at 16:48.

source.text: וְלֹא֩ בְחַ֨יִל גָּד֜וֹל וּבְקָהָ֣ל רָ֗ב יַעֲשֶׂ֨ה אוֹת֤וֹ פַרְעֹה֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה בִּשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ סֹלְלָ֖ה וּבִבְנ֣וֹת דָּיֵ֑ק לְהַכְרִ֖ית נְפָשׁ֥וֹת רַבּֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And not with a great army and a large company will Pharaoh deal with him in the war, when heaping up a ramp and building a siege wall to cut off many lives.

en.L: And Pharaoh, with a great army and a large company, will not act for him in the war, when a ramp is heaped up and a siege wall built to cut off many lives.
en.B: Pharaoh with his mighty army and great horde will not help him in battle, when ramps are heaped up and siege walls are built to destroy many lives.
en.R: Pharaoh and his great army will not help him in the war. The enemy will build ramps and siege walls and kill many people.

fr.L: Et le pharaon, avec une grande armée et une troupe nombreuse, n’agira pas pour lui dans la guerre, quand on élèvera une rampe et qu’on bâtira un mur de siège pour retrancher beaucoup de vies.
fr.B: Le pharaon, avec sa puissante armée et ses troupes nombreuses, ne lui viendra pas en aide dans la bataille, quand on élèvera des rampes et qu’on bâtira des murs de siège pour détruire beaucoup de vies.
fr.R: Le pharaon et sa grande armée ne l’aideront pas dans la guerre. L’ennemi construira des rampes et des murs de siège et tuera beaucoup de gens.

ko.L: 그리고 흙 언덕을 쌓고 포위 벽을 세워 많은 목숨을 끊으려 할 때에, 바로는 큰 군대와 많은 무리를 거느리고도 전쟁에서 그를 도와주지 않을 것이다.
ko.B: 적이 흙 언덕을 쌓고 포위 벽을 세워 많은 목숨을 없애려 할 때에, 바로가 강한 군대와 많은 무리를 거느리고 있어도 전쟁에서 그를 돕지 못할 것이다.
ko.R: 바로와 그의 큰 군대도 그 전쟁에서 그를 도와주지 못할 것이다. 적군이 흙 언덕과 포위 벽을 쌓고 많은 사람을 죽일 것이다.

decisions.choice: a ramp and a siege wall: the works of a siege
decisions.reason: An army besieging a city heaped up earth ramps against its walls and built a wall of its own around it (4:2; 2 Kings 25:1).

decisions.choice: Pharaoh will not help him: Egypt's help failed
decisions.reason: An Egyptian army came out during the siege, and the Babylonians withdrew for a time, but Jeremiah warned that Pharaoh's army would go home and the Babylonians would return, as they did (Jeremiah 37:5-11).

decisions.choice: The enemy will build
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say who builds the ramps; Readable makes plain that it is the attacking army.

decisions.choice: The siege clause ("when a ramp is heaped up…") comes first in Korean
decisions.reason: Korean puts the time clause before the main verb; the content stays within verse 17. "Pharaoh" is 바로, the published form.

source.text: וּבָזָ֥ה אָלָ֖ה לְהָפֵ֣ר בְּרִ֑ית וְהִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֥ן יָד֛וֹ וְכָל־אֵ֥לֶּה עָשָׂ֖ה לֹ֥א יִמָּלֵֽט׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he despised an oath by breaking a covenant; and look, he had given his hand, and all these he did; he will not escape.

en.L: For he despised the oath by breaking the covenant; and look, he had given his hand, yet all these [things] he did; he will not escape.
en.B: He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. Though he had given his hand on it, he did all these things. He will not escape.
en.R: He treated his promise as worthless and broke the agreement. He had given his hand to show that he would keep it, but he did all these things anyway. He will not escape.

fr.L: Car il a méprisé le serment en rompant l’alliance ; et voici, il avait donné sa main, et pourtant il a fait toutes ces [choses] ; il n’échappera pas.
fr.B: Il a méprisé le serment en rompant l’alliance. Alors qu’il s’y était engagé la main dans la main, il a fait tout cela. Il n’échappera pas.
fr.R: Il a traité sa promesse comme si elle ne valait rien et il a rompu l’accord. Il avait donné sa main pour montrer qu’il le respecterait, mais il a quand même fait toutes ces choses. Il n’échappera pas.

ko.L: 그는 언약을 깨뜨려 맹세를 업신여겼다. 보아라, 그가 손을 내밀어 [약속하고도] 이 모든 일을 했으니, 그는 피하지 못할 것이다.
ko.B: 그는 맹세를 업신여기고 언약을 깨뜨렸다. 손을 내밀어 약속해 놓고도 이 모든 짓을 했으니, 그는 결코 피하지 못할 것이다.
ko.R: 그는 자기 맹세를 하찮게 여기고 조약을 깨뜨렸다. 그는 손을 내밀어 그것을 지키겠다고 약속했지만, 그래도 이 모든 짓을 했다. 그는 벌을 피하지 못할 것이다.

decisions.choice: he had given his hand: he had pledged himself
decisions.reason: To give one's hand was a gesture that sealed a promise (2 Kings 10:15; Ezra 10:19).

source.text: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־אָמַ֨ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֮ חַי־אָנִי֒ אִם־לֹ֗א אָֽלָתִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּזָ֔ה וּבְרִיתִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵפִ֑יר וּנְתַתִּ֖יו בְּרֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: [As] I live, surely my oath which he despised and my covenant which he broke, I will bring it on his head.

en.L: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: [As] I live, surely {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} oath that he despised and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant that he broke, I will bring it on his head.
en.B: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: As surely as I live, I will make him bear the penalty of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} oath, which he despised, and of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, which he broke.
en.R: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: As surely as I live, he will pay for despising the promise he made in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name and for breaking the agreement he made before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : [Aussi vrai que] je suis vivant, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serment qu’il a méprisé et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} alliance qu’il a rompue, je les ferai retomber sur sa tête.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Aussi vrai que je suis vivant, je lui ferai porter la peine de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serment, qu’il a méprisé, et de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} alliance, qu’il a rompue.
fr.R: Alors voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Aussi vrai que je suis vivant, il paiera pour avoir méprisé la promesse qu’il a faite en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom et pour avoir rompu l’accord qu’il a conclu devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

ko.L: 그러므로 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 내가 살아 있음을 [두고 맹세한다]. 그가 업신여긴 내 맹세와 그가 깨뜨린 내 언약을 내가 반드시 그의 머리 위에 돌리겠다.
ko.B: 그러므로 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 내가 살아 있음을 두고 맹세한다. 그가 업신여긴 내 맹세와 그가 깨뜨린 내 언약의 벌을 내가 반드시 그에게 갚겠다.
ko.R: 그래서 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 내가 살아 있음을 두고 맹세한다. 그는 내 이름으로 한 맹세를 하찮게 여기고 내 앞에서 맺은 조약을 깨뜨렸다. 내가 반드시 그 대가를 치르게 하겠다.

decisions.choice: my oath ... my covenant: an oath sworn in the LORD's name was the LORD's
decisions.reason: Zedekiah swore by God when he made the treaty (2 Chronicles 36:13). So in breaking it he broke faith with the LORD himself, not only with Babylon (verse 20).

decisions.choice: I will bring it on his head: he will suffer the punishment the oath called down
decisions.reason: An oath called down a curse on the one who broke it. The LORD will see that the curse falls on Zedekiah (compare 16:43).

decisions.choice: the promise he made in my name ... the agreement he made before me
decisions.reason: Readable says why the oath and the covenant are called the LORD's (m1).

decisions.choice: The oath "as I live" as its own sentence after the formula
decisions.reason: As at 14:16: 내가 살아 있음을 두고 맹세한다 stands alone, and the sworn statement follows with 반드시.

source.text: וּפָרַשְׂתִּ֤י עָלָיו֙ רִשְׁתִּ֔י וְנִתְפַּ֖שׂ בִּמְצֽוּדָתִ֑י וַהֲבִיאוֹתִ֣יהוּ בָבֶ֗לָה וְנִשְׁפַּטְתִּ֤י אִתּוֹ֙ שָׁ֔ם מַעֲל֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָֽעַל־בִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will spread over him my net, and he will be caught in my snare; and I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there for his unfaithfulness which he committed against me.

en.L: And I will spread {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net over him, and he will be caught in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} snare; and I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there for his unfaithfulness that he committed against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: I will spread {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net over him, and he will be caught in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} snare. I will bring him to Babylon and judge him there for the unfaithfulness he committed against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: I will throw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net over him and catch him in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} trap. I will bring him to Babylon and judge him there, because he was unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

fr.L: Et j’étendrai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} filet sur lui, et il sera pris dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} piège ; je l’amènerai à Babylone et là j’entrerai en jugement avec lui pour l’infidélité qu’il a commise envers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: J’étendrai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} filet sur lui, et il sera pris dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} piège. Je l’emmènerai à Babylone et là je le jugerai pour l’infidélité qu’il a commise envers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Je lancerai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} filet sur lui et je l’attraperai dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} piège. Je l’emmènerai à Babylone et je le jugerai là-bas, parce qu’il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a été infidèle.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 내 그물을 그의 위에 펼칠 것이니, 그가 내 올무에 걸릴 것이다. 내가 그를 바빌론으로 데려가서, 그가 나에게 저지른 배신 때문에 거기에서 그를 심판하겠다.
ko.B: 내가 그 위에 내 그물을 펼치면 그가 내 올무에 걸릴 것이다. 내가 그를 바빌론으로 끌고 가서, 그가 나를 배신한 죄를 물어 거기에서 그를 심판하겠다.
ko.R: 내가 그에게 내 그물을 던져서 내 덫으로 그를 잡겠다. 내가 그를 바빌론으로 끌고 가서 거기에서 심판하겠다. 그가 나를 배신했기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: I will spread my net over him: the same words as 12:13
decisions.reason: Ezekiel has already said this of Zedekiah in 12:13, where the LORD says that he will bring him to Babylon, but he will not see it.

decisions.choice: unfaithfulness: a breach of trust against God
decisions.reason: The word *ma'al* means to act faithlessly, to betray what was entrusted (Leviticus 5:15; Ezekiel 14:13).

decisions.choice: "내 그물", "내 올무" (L, B), "내 덫" (R), worded as 12:13
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 12:13 word for word in Hebrew, so the Korean repeats that verse's wording.

source.text: וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־מִבְרָחָ֤יו בְּכָל־אֲגַפָּיו֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֔לוּ וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִ֖ים לְכָל־ר֣וּחַ יִפָּרֵ֑שׂוּ וִידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And all his fugitives among all his troops by the sword will fall, and those who remain to every wind will be scattered; and you will know that I, Yahweh, have spoken.

en.L: And all his fugitives among all his troops will fall by the sword, and the survivors will be scattered to every wind; and you will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.
en.B: All the fugitives from his troops will fall by the sword, and those who are left will be scattered in every direction. Then you will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.
en.R: All the soldiers who run away from his army will be killed in battle, and those who are left will be scattered in every direction. Then you will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.

fr.L: Et tous ses fuyards parmi toutes ses troupes tomberont par l’épée, et les survivants seront dispersés à tous les vents ; et vous saurez que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai parlé.
fr.B: Tous les fuyards de ses troupes tomberont par l’épée, et ceux qui resteront seront dispersés dans toutes les directions. Alors vous saurez que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai parlé.
fr.R: Tous les soldats qui s’enfuiront de son armée seront tués au combat, et ceux qui resteront seront dispersés dans toutes les directions. Alors vous saurez que c’est moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui l’ai dit.

ko.L: 그리고 그의 모든 군대 가운데서 도망한 자들은 모두 칼에 쓰러지고, 남은 자들은 사방의 바람에 흩어질 것이다. 그리고 너희는 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한 줄 알 것이다.
ko.B: 그의 군대에서 도망한 자들은 모두 칼에 쓰러지고, 살아남은 자들은 사방으로 흩어질 것이다. 그러면 너희는 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한 줄 알게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 그의 군대에서 도망치는 군인들은 모두 싸움터에서 죽고, 살아남은 자들은 사방으로 흩어질 것이다. 그러면 너희는 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한 줄 알게 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: his fugitives
decisions.reason: Many Hebrew manuscripts read "his choice men", which differs by one letter. The standard text, "his fugitives", fits the escape of Zedekiah's soldiers when the city fell (2 Kings 25:4-5).

decisions.choice: and you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken (L); Then you will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording, with "have spoken" added as the Hebrew has it.

decisions.choice: ’Moi, le SEIGNEUR, j’ai parlé’ (L, B); ’C’est moi, le SEIGNEUR, qui le dis’ (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The book’s term list; here inside ’you will know that’, so Readable says ’qui l’ai dit’.

source.text: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְלָקַ֣חְתִּי אָ֗נִי מִצַּמֶּ֧רֶת הָאֶ֛רֶז הָרָמָ֖ה וְנָתָ֑תִּי מֵרֹ֤אשׁ יֹֽנְקוֹתָיו֙ רַ֣ךְ אֶקְטֹ֔ף וְשָׁתַ֣לְתִּי אָ֔נִי עַ֥ל הַר־גָּבֹ֖הַ וְתָלֽוּל׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: And I myself will take from the top of the cedar, the high one, and set [it]; from the top of its young twigs a tender one I will pluck off, and I myself will plant [it] on a mountain high and lofty.

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will take [a sprig] from the top of the lofty cedar and set [it out]; from the topmost of its young twigs I will pluck off a tender one, and I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will plant [it] on a high and lofty mountain.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will take a sprig from the top of the tall cedar and plant it. I will pluck a tender shoot from its topmost twigs, and I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will take a small branch from the top of the tall cedar and plant it. I will break off a tender young shoot from its highest branches. I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will plant it on a very high mountain.

fr.L: Ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Moi-même, je prendrai [un rameau] de la cime du cèdre élevé et je [le] placerai ; de la cime de ses jeunes rameaux j’arracherai un tendre [rejeton], et {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}, je [le] planterai sur une montagne haute et élevée.
fr.B: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Moi-même, je prendrai un rameau à la cime du grand cèdre et je le planterai. J’arracherai une tendre pousse de ses plus hauts rameaux, et {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}, je la planterai sur une montagne haute et élevée.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Moi-même, je prendrai une petite branche à la cime du grand cèdre et je la planterai. Je casserai une jeune pousse toute tendre de ses plus hautes branches. Moi-même, je la planterai sur une très haute montagne.

ko.L: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 내가 친히 높은 백향목 꼭대기에서 [가지를] 가져다가 심겠다. 그 어린 가지들의 맨 꼭대기에서 연한 것을 꺾어, 내가 친히 높고 우뚝 솟은 산 위에 [그것을] 심겠다.
ko.B: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 내가 친히 높은 백향목 꼭대기에서 가지 하나를 가져다가 심겠다. 맨 꼭대기의 어린 가지들 가운데서 연한 싹을 꺾어, 내가 친히 높이 솟은 산 위에 심겠다.
ko.R: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 내가 직접 키 큰 백향목 꼭대기에서 작은 가지 하나를 가져다가 심겠다. 가장 높은 가지들에서 연한 어린싹을 꺾어서, 내가 직접 아주 높은 산 위에 심겠다.

decisions.choice: a tender shoot planted by the LORD: a future king from David's line
alternatives: the return of the exiles in general
decisions.reason: The LORD now acts in place of the eagles. From the same cedar, the royal house of David, he takes a shoot and plants it in Israel. The prophets use the same picture for the king to come from David's line: the shoot from the stump of Jesse (Isaiah 11:1) and the righteous Branch (Jeremiah 23:5; 33:15). Christians have read it of Jesus as the son of David. The text names no king.

decisions.choice: I myself: the "I" is emphatic
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds "I" to the verbs, setting the LORD's planting against the eagle's in verse 3.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula.

decisions.choice: ’Moi-même, je …’ for the emphatic ’I’; at the start of a sentence written plainly with its capital, inside one under deity_pronoun (’et moi-même/Moi-même, je planterai’)
decisions.reason: French marks the emphatic pronoun with ’moi-même’; the style guide writes a pronoun at the start of a sentence with its capital and no span.

decisions.choice: "친히" (L, B), "직접" (R) for the emphatic "I myself"
decisions.reason: As 14:4; God speaks of himself without -시-, so the emphasis rests on the adverb.

source.text: בְּהַ֨ר מְר֤וֹם יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶשְׁתֳּלֶ֔נּוּ וְנָשָׂ֤א עָנָף֙ וְעָ֣שָׂה פֶ֔רִי וְהָיָ֖ה לְאֶ֣רֶז אַדִּ֑יר וְשָׁכְנ֣וּ תַחְתָּ֗יו כֹּ֚ל צִפּ֣וֹר כָּל־כָּנָ֔ף בְּצֵ֥ל דָּלִיּוֹתָ֖יו תִּשְׁכֹּֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: On [the] mountain of [the] height of Israel I will plant it, and it will lift up branches and produce fruit and become a majestic cedar; and under it will dwell every bird of every wing; in the shade of its branches they will dwell.

en.L: On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it, and it will bear branches and produce fruit and become a majestic cedar; and under it will dwell every bird of every wing; in the shade of its branches they will dwell.
en.B: On the high mountain of Israel I will plant it, and it will put out branches and bear fruit, and it will become a majestic cedar. Birds of every kind will live under it; they will find shelter in the shade of its branches.
en.R: I will plant it on Israel's highest mountain. It will grow branches and produce fruit. It will become a great cedar tree. All kinds of birds will live under it and find shelter in the shade of its branches.

fr.L: Sur la montagne élevée d’Israël je le planterai, et il portera des rameaux et produira du fruit, et il deviendra un cèdre magnifique ; sous lui habiteront tous les oiseaux de toute aile ; à l’ombre de ses branches ils habiteront.
fr.B: Sur la haute montagne d’Israël je le planterai, et il poussera des rameaux, portera du fruit et deviendra un cèdre magnifique. Les oiseaux de toute espèce habiteront sous lui ; ils trouveront abri à l’ombre de ses branches.
fr.R: Je le planterai sur la plus haute montagne d’Israël. Il fera des branches et produira des fruits. Il deviendra un grand cèdre. Toutes sortes d’oiseaux vivront sous lui et trouveront un abri à l’ombre de ses branches.

ko.L: 이스라엘의 높은 산 위에 내가 그것을 심겠다. 그러면 그것이 가지를 내고 열매를 맺어 훌륭한 백향목이 될 것이다. 온갖 날개 달린 온갖 새가 그 아래에 깃들이고, 그 가지들의 그늘에 깃들일 것이다.
ko.B: 이스라엘의 높은 산에 내가 그것을 심겠다. 그러면 그것이 가지를 뻗고 열매를 맺어 훌륭한 백향목이 될 것이다. 온갖 새가 그 아래에 깃들이고, 그 가지들의 그늘에서 쉴 곳을 찾을 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 그것을 이스라엘의 가장 높은 산에 심겠다. 그것은 가지를 내고 열매를 맺을 것이다. 그리고 큰 백향목이 될 것이다. 온갖 새가 그 아래에 살고, 그 가지들의 그늘에서 쉴 것이다.

decisions.choice: the mountain height of Israel: Mount Zion
decisions.reason: Ezekiel uses the phrase for the mountain where Israel will worship the LORD (20:40). The prophets picture this mountain raised above all others (Isaiah 2:2; Micah 4:1).

decisions.choice: birds of every kind under its branches: many peoples finding shelter
decisions.reason: A great tree with birds in its branches pictures a kingdom that shelters many peoples (31:6; Daniel 4:9). Jesus uses the picture in the parable of the mustard seed (Matthew 13:32).

source.text: וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כָּל־עֲצֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ הִשְׁפַּ֣לְתִּי׀עֵ֣ץ גָּבֹ֗הַ הִגְבַּ֨הְתִּי֙ עֵ֣ץ שָׁפָ֔ל הוֹבַ֨שְׁתִּי֙ עֵ֣ץ לָ֔ח וְהִפְרַ֖חְתִּי עֵ֣ץ יָבֵ֑שׁ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִֽׂיתִי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And all the trees of the field will know that I, Yahweh, bring low a high tree, make high a low tree, dry up a green tree and make a dry tree sprout. I, Yahweh, have spoken and will do [it].

en.L: And all the trees of the field will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, bring low the high tree [and] make high the low tree, dry up the green tree and make the dry tree sprout. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken, and I will do [it].
en.B: All the trees of the field will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, bring down the tall tree and raise up the low tree, dry up the green tree and make the dry tree flourish. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken, and I will do it.
en.R: Then all the trees in the field will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, cut down tall trees and make small trees grow tall. I dry up green trees and make dry trees grow green. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken, and I will do it.

fr.L: Et tous les arbres des champs sauront que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’abaisse l’arbre élevé [et] j’élève l’arbre bas, je fais sécher l’arbre vert et je fais bourgeonner l’arbre sec. Moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai parlé, et je [le] ferai.
fr.B: Tous les arbres des champs sauront que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’abaisse l’arbre élevé et j’élève l’arbre bas, je dessèche l’arbre vert et je fais reverdir l’arbre sec. Moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai parlé, et je le ferai.
fr.R: Alors tous les arbres des champs sauront que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’abats les grands arbres et je fais grandir les petits. Je dessèche les arbres verts et je fais reverdir les arbres secs. C’est moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui le dis, et je le ferai.

ko.L: 그리고 들의 모든 나무가 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 높은 나무를 낮추고 낮은 나무를 높이며, 푸른 나무를 말리고 마른 나무를 싹 트게 하는 줄 알 것이다. 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말하였고, [그대로] 행하겠다.
ko.B: 들의 모든 나무가 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 높은 나무를 낮추고 낮은 나무를 높이며, 푸른 나무를 말리고 마른 나무에 싹이 돋게 하는 줄 알게 될 것이다. 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말했으니 그대로 이루겠다.
ko.R: 그때에 들에 있는 모든 나무가 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 큰 나무를 베어 넘어뜨리고 작은 나무를 크게 자라게 하는 줄 알게 될 것이다. 나는 푸른 나무를 말리고 마른 나무를 다시 푸르게 한다. 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말했으니 그대로 이루겠다.

decisions.choice: all the trees of the field: the nations and their kings
decisions.reason: In the picture of the chapter, trees stand for kings and nations (31:3-9). They will see that the LORD decides who rises and who falls.

decisions.choice: I bring low the high tree and make high the low tree: the LORD reverses human greatness
decisions.reason: The same reversal is praised in Hannah's prayer (1 Samuel 2:7-8) and in Mary's song (Luke 1:52). Here the proud cedar of Jerusalem's kings was cut down, and the LORD will raise up a lowly shoot.

decisions.choice: "나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말하였고, [그대로] 행하겠다" (L), "나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말했으니 그대로 이루겠다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for "I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it"; God names himself with 나 and no -시-.
